target_customer: Consumers seeking on-demand mental health support, plus therapists wanting tools to grow their practices
problem: Access to therapy and coaching is fragmented; Plutis combined AI journaling and coaching, licensed therapists and peer support groups in one app.
business_model: Consumer app, listed free on iOS with services through therapists and coaches (pricing not verified)

founders.name: Kamil Ali
previous_startups: AccessBell (white-label telemedicine video platform, acquired by its largest customer Tata Group)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. Education not found.

founders.name: Asim Hirji
previous_startups: AccessBell (white-label telemedicine video platform, acquired by its largest customer Tata Group)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. Education not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: A consumer app with chat, journaling and an LLM wrapper is standard mobile engineering; matching with therapists is operational.

defensibility.rationale: Consumer journaling and AI coaching features were easy to copy and crowded by funded mental health apps.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents acting on Plutis; listed only as category incumbents without a source.

market_need_then: Demand for digital mental health was high after the pandemic; the founders had prior telemedicine experience. No product-specific demand evidence was found.

branding.domain_note: plutis.io currently appears to show a different POS product named Market Leap, so the original domain may have been repurposed or lost.

identity.voice_and_tone: Personal and supportive per the YC bio

branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt launch on 2023-09-05 with 417 followers.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand coverage; the name resembles Plutus and Plutio, which dominate search results.

outcome_analysis: Plutis launched an iOS app in 2023 and a Product Hunt page in September 2023, and no funding, acquisition or shutdown could be verified. One tracker says the Android app left Google Play in July 2024 and the current plutis.io page shows an unrelated POS product, suggesting it stalled, but this is not confirmed and the cause is not public.
notes: YC directory says Active, but evidence of activity after 2023 is thin. A third-party tracker claims removal from Google Play on 2024-07-07 (single source, unverified). plutis.io fetch showed Market Leap POS content, and a G2 page describes plutis.io as a financial services company, so the domain may belong to different businesses. No funding found. Exit type unknown. No dated competitor source found.
